## Scope {.unnumbered}

This is the fully parametric model that the whole investigation points to, and the EM that fits it. It
keeps the one thing we validated empirically — **the ambient is Poisson conditional on the cell's soup
depth, whether or not the guide is present** ([`doublet_overdispersion.html`](doublet_overdispersion.html))
— and adds a parametric, overdispersed **signal** layer. fishash, CLEANSER, geomux and our depth_fix all
fall out as special cases (§Special cases). Companion: [`literature_review.html`](literature_review.html)
(the method landscape and the two-strategies / EM unification this model formalizes).

---

## The model {#sec-model}

Guides $g=1,\dots,G$, cells $c=1,\dots,C$. A latent **integration indicator** $X_{g,c}\in\{0,1\}$ says
whether guide $g$ is truly in cell $c$. The observed count is **ambient molecules plus (if integrated)
native molecules, both captured** — a sum, not a replacement:
$$
\boxed{\;N_{g,c}=Z_{g,c}+X_{g,c}\,W_{g,c},\qquad
Z_{g,c}\sim\mathrm{Poisson}(a_g d_c),\quad
W_{g,c}\sim\mathrm{NB}(\mu_g s_c,\theta),\quad
X_{g,c}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\pi_g),\;}
$$
all independent, with $\mathrm{NB}(m,\theta)$ meaning mean $m$, size $\theta$, $\mathrm{Var}=m+m^2/\theta$.

The **ambient layer $Z$ is always on and always Poisson** — the soup deposits its contribution in every
droplet. The **signal layer $W$ is gated by $X$ and is negative-binomial** — native counts vary
cell-to-cell (copy number, expression), so they are overdispersed. Hence the two hypotheses are
$$
N_{g,c}\mid X_{g,c}{=}0\ \sim\ \mathrm{Poisson}(a_g d_c),
\qquad
N_{g,c}\mid X_{g,c}{=}1\ \sim\ \mathrm{Poisson}(a_g d_c)\ \circledast\ \mathrm{NB}(\mu_g s_c,\theta),
$$
a **convolution** under the alternative — **not** $\mathrm{NB}(a_gd_c+\mu_gs_c,\theta)$, which would
(wrongly) let the ambient turn overdispersed when the guide is present.

**Poisson–Gamma form (the cleanest statement that "ambient stays Poisson").** Writing the NB as a
Poisson–Gamma mixture, $W_{g,c}=\mathrm{Poisson}(\mu_g s_c\,U_{g,c})$ with $U_{g,c}\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(\theta,\theta)$
(mean 1, variance $1/\theta$),
$$
N_{g,c}\mid X_{g,c},U_{g,c}\ \sim\ \mathrm{Poisson}\big(\underbrace{a_g d_c}_{\text{Poisson offset, no }U}+\;X_{g,c}\,\underbrace{\mu_g s_c\,U_{g,c}}_{\text{overdispersed signal}}\big).
$$
The dispersion $U$ multiplies **only** the signal rate; the ambient rate $a_gd_c$ is a fixed Poisson
offset under both $X=0$ and $X=1$. That is exactly what "ambient is Poisson even under the alternative"
means, and it matters precisely in the **low-separation regime** ($\mu_gs_c$ not $\gg a_gd_c$) where
assignment is hard; at high separation the convolution and $\mathrm{NB}(a_gd_c+\mu_gs_c)$ coincide.

### Parameters, gauges, identifiability {#sec-params}

| symbol | meaning | stratum it is learned from |
|---|---|---|
| $a_g$ | ambient soup profile (guide share), $\sum_g a_g=1$ | noise ($X{=}0$) |
| $d_c$ | cell **ambient exposure** (soup depth) | noise ($X{=}0$) |
| $\mu_g$ | guide native expression/capture strength | signal ($X{=}1$) |
| $s_c$ | cell **native-capture depth** | signal ($X{=}1$) |
| $\theta$ | signal dispersion (Poisson as $\theta\to\infty$) | signal residuals |
| $\pi_g$ | integration prevalence ($\propto$ MOI × representation) | responsibilities |

Two rank-1 rate fields, each with a guide factor and a cell factor. **Gauges:** $\sum_g a_g=1$ fixes the
ambient scale (so $d_c$ carries ambient magnitude); a matching normalization on $\mu$ or $s$ fixes the
signal scale. **The two per-cell depths are distinct and separately identified** because they are
estimated from **disjoint strata** — $d_c$ from cells/entries where the guide is absent, $s_c$ from where
it is present — and empirically $s_c\gg d_c$ (native capture dominates library size, so $N_{:,c}\approx
\mu_{g^\*}s_c\gg d_c$: "library size $\approx s_c$, not $d_c$"). Exogenous/barcode-swap noise, if modeled,
is a second Poisson term folded into $a_gd_c$ (still "not signal, and Poisson").

*Empirical status:* the ambient-Poisson layer is not assumed — it is validated on the real barnyard by a
bootstrap-calibrated goodness-of-fit ($\hat\phi=0.99$ inside the Poisson null band;
[`doublet_overdispersion.html`](doublet_overdispersion.html) §Part 4), and it is the same assumption as
CellBender's $N^{\text{endo}}\sim\mathrm{Poisson}$ layer.

### The ambient profile tracks native abundance (empirical) {#sec-ambient-tracks}

We keep $a_g$ a **free parameter**, MLE'd from the noise stratum ($X{=}0$ entries) by M-step 1 — we do
**not** couple it to the signal parameters $(\mu_g,\pi_g)$ or impose any prior on it, so the method stays
frequentist. Nonetheless there is a clean empirical regularity worth recording: **the ambient soup
profile tracks the native abundance,** $a_g\approx\kappa\,\pi_g\mu_g$ for a shared constant $\kappa$.
Measured cross-species on the de-doubleted barnyard (a guide's ambient share in wrong-species cells vs its
native share in own-species cells), the relationship is tight — slope $\approx 1$, correlation
$r\approx 0.95$ on direct-capture. The residual ~2× per-guide scatter is mostly sampling noise: split-half
reproducibility is ICC $\approx 0.35$ (so ~60–65% of it is per-cell Poisson sampling, confirmed against
the Poisson floor), and the reproducible ~35% does **not** persist across runs (0 hr vs 72 hr residual
correlation $\approx 0$) — i.e. it is a per-run finite-soup-draw realization (~1.25× fold), not a stable
guide-intrinsic effect. So $a_g\propto\pi_g\mu_g$ holds **in expectation**; the deviations are sampling at
two levels (per-cell capture + per-run soup formation).

This is a validated empirical fact, not a modeling assumption, and it earns its keep in three
non-Bayesian ways ($a_g$ stays a free MLE throughout):

1. **EM initialization.** Warm-start $a_g^{(0)}=\pi_g\mu_g$ from a rough threshold assignment; the ambient
   layer then converges faster and more stably than from a blind start.
2. **Diagnostic / goodness-of-fit.** The fitted $\hat a_g$ should track $\pi_g\mu_g$ to within ~1.25×; a
   gross departure flags a problem (residual doublets, a mis-specified guide, a QC issue).
3. **Mechanistic origin of the guide-margin (Simpson) contamination.** Because the ambient composition
   equals the native composition, the raw guide margin $N_{g,:}$ is signal-contaminated **by
   construction** — which is exactly why $a_g$ must be estimated from the noise stratum ($X{=}0$ entries),
   not the raw margin. This is the generative reason fishash's Simpson correction exists.

---

## Likelihood {#sec-likelihood}

Let $f_0(n)=\mathrm{Pois}(n;a_gd_c)$ and $f_1(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\mathrm{Pois}(k;a_gd_c)\,\mathrm{NB}(n-k;\mu_gs_c,\theta)$
be the null and alternative densities at $(g,c)$ (the latter the convolution). The **observed-data
log-likelihood** is a mixture,
$$
\ell(\Theta)=\sum_{g,c}\log\!\Big[(1-\pi_g)\,f_0(N_{g,c})+\pi_g\,f_1(N_{g,c})\Big],\qquad
\Theta=\big(\{a_g\},\{d_c\},\{\mu_g\},\{s_c\},\theta,\{\pi_g\}\big).
$$
Direct maximization is awkward (the convolution couples the layers); the latent structure makes **EM**
the natural route.

---

## Fitting by EM {#sec-em}

Augment with $X_{g,c}$ and, within the signal component, the Poisson–Gamma scale $U_{g,c}$ and the
**split** $N_{g,c}=Z_{g,c}+W_{g,c}$. The key fact that makes the split tractable: given $X{=}1$ and $U$,
$Z$ and $W$ are independent Poissons summing to $N$, so
$$
Z_{g,c}\mid N_{g,c},X{=}1,U_{g,c}\ \sim\ \mathrm{Binomial}\!\Big(N_{g,c},\ \tfrac{a_gd_c}{a_gd_c+\mu_gs_cU_{g,c}}\Big)
$$
(Poisson thinning). Ambient and signal are thereby fit on cleanly separated expected counts.

### E-step {#sec-estep}

At the current $\Theta$:

- **Responsibility** (the calibrated soft assignment):
$$
r_{g,c}=\Pr(X_{g,c}{=}1\mid N_{g,c})=\frac{\pi_g\,f_1(N_{g,c})}{(1-\pi_g)\,f_0(N_{g,c})+\pi_g\,f_1(N_{g,c})}.
$$
- **Expected ambient/signal split.** With
  $\;e_{g,c}:=\mathbb E[Z_{g,c}\mid N_{g,c},X{=}1]=\dfrac{1}{f_1(N_{g,c})}\sum_{k=0}^{N_{g,c}}k\,\mathrm{Pois}(k;a_gd_c)\,\mathrm{NB}(N_{g,c}-k;\mu_gs_c,\theta)$,
  the **expected ambient count** (used to fit the ambient layer) and **expected signal count** (used to
  fit the signal layer) are
$$
\widetilde Z_{g,c}=(1-r_{g,c})\,N_{g,c}+r_{g,c}\,e_{g,c},
\qquad
\widetilde W_{g,c}=r_{g,c}\,\big(N_{g,c}-e_{g,c}\big).
$$
  (In noise cells all of $N$ is ambient; in signal cells only the small imputed part $e_{g,c}$ is.)
- **Dispersion sufficient statistics** $\mathbb E[U_{g,c}\mid N,X{=}1]$ and
  $\mathbb E[\log U_{g,c}\mid N,X{=}1]$ for the $\theta$ update (or defer to a residual estimator, below).

Because $a_gd_c$ is tiny, the sums over $k$ truncate at $k=1$–$2$: the convolution and split are cheap.

### M-step {#sec-mstep}

Each layer is a recognizable fit on its expected counts:

1. **Ambient — rank-1 Poisson MLE of $\widetilde Z$.** The independence/rank-1 fit is the margin product,
$$
\hat a_g\hat d_c=\frac{\big(\textstyle\sum_c\widetilde Z_{g,c}\big)\big(\sum_g\widetilde Z_{g,c}\big)}{\sum_{g,c}\widetilde Z_{g,c}},
\qquad\text{gauge }\ \hat a_g=\frac{\sum_c\widetilde Z_{g,c}}{\sum_{g,c}\widetilde Z_{g,c}},\ \ \hat d_c=\textstyle\sum_g\widetilde Z_{g,c}.
$$
   This is fishash's rank-1 completion with **soft** weights — and it yields the **decontaminated ambient
   depth $\hat d_c$** (the depth_fix quantity), because signal cells contribute only their imputed ambient
   $e_{g,c}$, not their signal.
2. **Signal — rank-1 NB GLM of $\widetilde W$** with log-mean $\log\mu_g+\log s_c$ (and the known offset
   $a_gd_c$ where you keep the exact convolution). Fit by IRLS; in the $\theta\to\infty$ (Poisson) limit it
   reduces to the same weighted-margin update as the ambient layer,
$$
\hat\mu_g\hat s_c\ \approx\ \frac{\big(\textstyle\sum_c\widetilde W_{g,c}\big)\big(\sum_g\widetilde W_{g,c}\big)}{\sum_{g,c}\widetilde W_{g,c}} .
$$
3. **Dispersion $\theta$** — Gamma MLE from $\mathbb E[U],\mathbb E[\log U]$, or a robust
   method-of-moments on the signal-stratum Pearson residuals
   $(N_{g,c}-\hat\mu_g\hat s_c)^2/\hat\mu_g\hat s_c$ weighted by $r_{g,c}$. May be shared or per-guide
   ($\theta_g$).
4. **Prevalence** $\hat\pi_g=\frac1C\sum_c r_{g,c}$.

Iterate E/M to convergence.

### The high-separation simplification {#sec-approx}

Where $r_{g,c}$ is large, $\mu_gs_c\gg a_gd_c$, so $e_{g,c}\approx a_gd_c$ (negligible) and
$\widetilde W_{g,c}\approx r_{g,c}N_{g,c}$. Then the offset drops and the signal component is a plain NB
with $U\mid N\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(\theta+N,\theta+\mu_gs_c)$ conjugate updates
$\mathbb E[U\mid N]=(\theta+N)/(\theta+\mu_gs_c)$. This is the practical recipe for direct-capture (huge
separation); keep the exact convolution for tight CROP-seq / weak-signal regimes.

---

## Assignment and error control {#sec-assign}

Error control is frequentist: a one-sided test of $H_0:X_{g,c}{=}0$ against the rank-1 ambient null. In
**unconditional (plug-in) form** this is the Poisson upper tail the family shares,
$$
p_{g,c}=\Pr\{\mathrm{Pois}(\hat a_g\hat d_c)\ge N_{g,c}\},
$$
corrected by **Guo–Sarkar** (tests within a cell as a dependent block) or BH — it needs only the fitted
null. The **implemented** methods (fishash, geomux, depth_fix) use the equivalent **margin-conditional**
form — a one-sided Fisher / hypergeometric test on the $2\times2$ contingency table {guide $g$ vs rest} ×
{cell $c$ vs rest}, with fishash's noise-conditioned background giving the adjusted odds ratio $R^\*$
(Eq 7); conditioning the rank-1 Poisson table on its margins is exactly what makes the two forms agree
(see §The two reduced EMs → Reduction B). When the signal layer is fit, the responsibility $r_{g,c}$ is
available as a plug-in **score** (assign where $r_{g,c}\ge 1-q$, i.e. threshold the plug-in
$1-r_{g,c}$), but the reported guarantee is the $p$-value / GS rule, not a posterior. One knob ($q$).

---

## Special cases {#sec-special}

Every method we benchmarked is this model with a layer dropped, a component non-parametric, or the E-step
hardened:

| method | ambient layer | signal layer | E-step | fit scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| geomux / bare ambient | rank-1 Poisson, **raw margins** | none | — (1 pass) | shared |
| **fishash** | rank-1 Poisson, denoised (masked) | **none** — omnibus upper-tail | **hard** | shared |
| **depth_fix (ours)** | rank-1 Poisson, denoised $\hat d_c$ | none — upper-tail | hard | shared |
| CLEANSER | Poisson/NB, $L_i$ depth | NB | soft (MCMC) | **per-guide** |
| **this model** | rank-1 Poisson, denoised $\hat d_c$ | **rank-1 NB $(\mu_gs_c,\theta)$** | **soft** | shared |

- **fishash / depth_fix** $=$ freeze the signal layer to the non-parametric alternative "$N_{g,c}$ exceeds
  the ambient Poisson tail" (equivalently $\theta$-agnostic) and harden the E-step to a 0/1 FDR call.
  depth_fix additionally uses the denoised $\hat d_c$ — which this model produces automatically in M-step 1.
- **CLEANSER** $=$ the same two layers but fit **per guide** (no shared rank-1) with a hard-cutoff depth
  $L_i$; this model shares the rank-1 across guides and decontaminates the depth in the fit.

So the parametric signal layer is what fishash gives up (for omnibus robustness) and CLEANSER has (but
per-guide). Adding it, **shared**, buys: strength-borrowing on $(\mu_g,s_c)$ so weak $(g,c)$ get a
calibrated signal expectation (power in the overlap regime), an NB $\theta$ that absorbs signal
overdispersion, and a genuine soft score. The costs are the NB/rank-1 signal assumptions and EM
initialization — but **not** the convolution, which no reduction ever evaluates (next).

### Neither reduction evaluates the convolution {#sec-noconv}

The Poisson$\circledast$NB convolution lives only in the alternative $f_1$, and $f_1$ is needed only for
the responsibility $r_{g,c}$ and for fitting the signal parameters. Both practical methods sidestep it:

- **fishash / depth_fix — never form $f_1$.** A one-sided test of $H_0:X_{g,c}{=}0$ ("is $N_{g,c}$ large
  under $\mathrm{Pois}(\hat a_g\hat d_c)$?") uses only the **null** $f_0$; the alternative — and thus the
  convolution — is never constructed. It loses little because ambient $\ll$ signal in signal cells, so the
  alternative *is* essentially "$N$ above the Poisson tail," which is exactly what the test detects.
- **The NB-mixture variant — approximate $f_1$ by dropping the offset.** Since $a_gd_c\ll\mu_gs_c$ in a
  cell that carries $g$,
$$
f_1(n)=\mathrm{Pois}(a_gd_c)\circledast\mathrm{NB}(\mu_gs_c,\theta)\ \approx\ \mathrm{NB}(\mu_gs_c,\theta),\qquad\text{error }O\!\big(a_gd_c/\mu_gs_c\big),
$$
  a sub-percent shift on direct-capture (a few percent on CROP-seq). The two components are then a plain
  $\{\mathrm{Poisson}(a_gd_c),\ \mathrm{NB}(\mu_gs_c)\}$ mixture — CLEANSER's form, here with the shared,
  denoised ambient — and the EM runs with no convolution.

So the convolution is the mechanistically-honest object but a computational non-issue: it is only
non-negligible in the vanishing-separation limit ($\mu_gs_c\sim a_gd_c$), exactly where the guide is
barely detectable and the correction is second-order. **The generative model contains a convolution; no
useful method has to evaluate one.**

---

## The two reduced EMs, written out {#sec-reduced-ems}

§Special cases named two reductions; here are the actual E/M loops each one collapses to. The thing the
**full** EM (§Fitting by EM) needs that both reductions exist to avoid is the convolution $f_1$, which
appears in exactly two places — the responsibility $r_{g,c}$ and the **thinning split**
$e_{g,c}=\mathbb E[Z_{g,c}\mid N,X{=}1]$ that lets a signal cell donate its imputed ambient part back to the
ambient fit. Remove the convolution and the split goes with it; the only latent variable left is the
indicator $X_{g,c}$.

### Reduction A — alternative $\approx$ NB: a two-component mixture-of-GLMs EM {#sec-em-nb}

Drop the ambient offset under the alternative, $f_1(n)\approx\mathrm{NB}(n;\mu_gs_c,\theta)$ (error
$O(a_gd_c/\mu_gs_c)$, §Neither reduction). Every entry is now *either* fully ambient *or* fully signal —
there is no per-entry $Z{+}W$ decomposition, so $e_{g,c}$ vanishes. This is a textbook per-entry mixture of
a Poisson and an NB with rank-1 rates. It is **CLEANSER's Poisson-vs-NB mixture**, with two changes: the
two rate fields are **shared rank-1** across guides (weak $(g,c)$ borrow strength) rather than fit per
guide, and the ambient depth is the **decontaminated $\hat d_c$** below rather than a hard-cutoff $L_i$.

**E-step** (densities only — no $k$-sums, no thinning):
$$
r_{g,c}=\frac{\pi_g\,\mathrm{NB}(N_{g,c};\mu_gs_c,\theta)}
{(1-\pi_g)\,\mathrm{Pois}(N_{g,c};a_gd_c)+\pi_g\,\mathrm{NB}(N_{g,c};\mu_gs_c,\theta)}.
$$

**M-step** — each entry donates its **whole** count $N_{g,c}$ to *both* layers, weighted by $1-r$ and $r$:

1. **Ambient — $(1-r)$-weighted rank-1 Poisson.** Maximizing $\sum_{g,c}(1-r_{g,c})[N\log(a_gd_c)-a_gd_c]$
   has no closed form (the weights now sit on the $-a_gd_c$ term), so it is a weighted Sinkhorn / IPF
   fixed point,
$$
\hat a_g=\frac{\sum_c(1-r_{g,c})N_{g,c}}{\sum_c(1-r_{g,c})\hat d_c},\qquad
\hat d_c=\frac{\sum_g(1-r_{g,c})N_{g,c}}{\sum_g(1-r_{g,c})\hat a_g},
$$
   alternated to convergence. This is where decontamination happens — and it is *cleaner* than the full
   model's M-step 1: signal entries carry weight $1-r\to0$ and are **excluded** from the depth fit, rather
   than folded back in through their imputed ambient $e_{g,c}$. The output $\hat d_c$ is the depth_fix
   ambient depth.
2. **Signal — $r$-weighted rank-1 NB GLM** with log-mean $\log\mu_g+\log s_c$, by weighted IRLS;
   $\hat\mu_g\hat s_c$ is the weighted margin product in the $\theta\to\infty$ limit.
3. **Dispersion $\theta$** — $r$-weighted NB/Gamma MLE (or $r$-weighted Pearson-residual MoM); shared or
   $\theta_g$.
4. **Prevalence** $\hat\pi_g=\frac1C\sum_c r_{g,c}$.

The convolution and thinning are gone; the price is the NB/rank-1 signal assumptions plus the
$(1-r)$-weighted IPF ambient step replacing the full model's closed-form margin product. This is the
smallest step up from depth_fix that buys a genuine soft score and power in the overlap regime.

### Reduction B — fishash-type: never fit the alternative, estimate the null properly {#sec-em-fishash}

Refuse to build $f_1$ at all: there is no $\pi_g,\mu_g,\theta$, only the null $(a_g,d_c)$. With no
alternative density the soft responsibility cannot be formed, so it is **replaced by a frequentist test**
and the EM degenerates into a hard-assignment masking loop (fishash Alg 1 / depth_fix).

**Hard E-step** — with no $f_1$ to form a likelihood ratio, the responsibility hardens to a 0/1 mask via a
**frequentist test on the $2\times2$ contingency table** $\{$guide $g$ vs the rest$\}\times\{$cell $c$ vs
the rest$\}$ — is $N_{g,c}$ larger than the rank-1 (independence) expectation? This is a one-sided
**Fisher / noncentral-hypergeometric** tail, **not** a Poisson tail. fishash's one move is to **denoise the
background (other-cells) entries** of the table with the noise-only counts from the current rank-1
completion, giving the adjusted odds ratio $R^\*$ (fishash Eq 7); rejecting at GS/BH level $q$ sets
$\hat X_{g,c}=1$:
$$
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 & \text{cell }c & \text{other cells}\\\hline
\text{guide }g & N_{g,c} & \text{(noise-only, denoised)}\\
\text{other guides} & N_{\cdot,c}-N_{g,c} & \cdots
\end{array}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
p_{g,c}=\Pr_{\mathrm{Hypergeom}}\big\{\ \ge N_{g,c}\ \big|\ \text{margins}\big\}.
$$
The threshold is the test's critical value, not a likelihood ratio (there is no $f_1$ to ratio against).

**Same null as §Assignment's Poisson tail — conditional vs unconditional.** Conditioning the rank-1
independent-Poisson table on its margins yields *exactly* the central hypergeometric, so the Fisher tail
(margin-conditional) and the plug-in $\Pr\{\mathrm{Pois}(\hat a_g\hat d_c)\ge N_{g,c}\}$ (unconditional)
test the identical rank-1-independence hypothesis — fishash / geomux / depth_fix all implement the
**conditional (table)** form. The M-step's "estimate the null properly" (rank-1 completion of the masked
matrix) is the Poisson-parametrization image of denoising the table's background cells. And **depth_fix is
this same hypergeometric test with the cell-margin "draws" set to the denoised ambient depth $\hat d_c$
instead of the raw library size $N_{\cdot,c}$** (fishash Eq 7 uses $N_{\cdot,c}$).

**M-step — null only, on the masked matrix.** Re-fit the rank-1 Poisson ambient with the $\hat X{=}1$
entries held out (matrix completion / `impute_masked_counts`):
$$
\hat a_g\hat d_c \;=\; \text{rank-1 Poisson completion of }\ \{N_{g,c}:\hat X_{g,c}=0\}.
$$
"Estimate stuff properly" lives entirely here: the **mask schedule** (fresh mask for $i\le3$, monotone-AND
after) keeps signal out of the ambient fit and prevents the degenerate fixed point, and depth_fix's single
addition is to *use* the resulting $\hat d_c$ as the null exposure in place of the raw library size
$N_{:,c}$. There is no signal M-step, no $r\in(0,1)$, no convolution: you only ever ask "is $N$ above the
ambient tail," never "how big is the signal."

### The two next to the full EM {#sec-em-compare}

| | latent modeled | E-step | signal M-step | convolution / split |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Full EM** (§Fitting) | $X$, $Z{=}W$ split, $U$ | soft $r$ + thinning $e_{g,c}$ | rank-1 NB with offset | yes (in E-step) |
| **A — NB-approx** | $X$ only | soft $r$, densities only | rank-1 NB, no offset | **gone** |
| **B — fishash** | $X$ only, hardened | hypergeometric table test $\to$ 0/1 mask | **none** | **gone** |

Top-to-bottom is a controlled degradation of one object: **A** drops the convolution and the thinning
split but keeps a soft mixture with a fitted alternative; **B** additionally freezes the alternative to
"upper tail" and hardens the E-step to an FDR call. B is *nearly* the $\theta\to\infty$, hard-$r$ limit of
A — the one nuance is that A still fits $\mu_gs_c$ (which in that limit only positions the likelihood-ratio
threshold, the role B's test critical value plays), whereas B never fits it at all. This is the reduction
behind recipe-step-4's sanity check ($\theta\to\infty$ + hard E-step $\Rightarrow$ depth_fix).

---

## Practical recipe {#sec-recipe}

1. **Initialize** the ambient layer with one depth_fix / fishash pass (rank-1 masked Poisson) → $\hat a_g,
   \hat d_c$ and an initial hard $X$; initialize the signal layer by a rank-1 NB fit to $N$ on the
   $X{=}1$ cells; set $\pi_g$ from the initial $X$.
2. **Iterate** E/M (§§E-step, M-step) ~5–10 times; use the high-separation simplification unless signal is
   weak.
3. **Assign** by the Poisson-null $p$-value + Guo–Sarkar/BH at level $q$ (the $r_{g,c}\ge 1-q$ plug-in is an optional score).
4. **Reductions to sanity-check the code:** $\theta\to\infty$ + hard E-step should reproduce depth_fix;
   raw margins + no E-step iteration should reproduce geomux/the bare ambient test.

The model is exactly as parametric as the data support: the ambient layer is empirically Poisson
(validated), the signal layer is where overdispersion is allowed to live, and the two per-cell depths
$d_c\neq s_c$ are what make the null exposure ($\hat d_c$) different from the library size — the reason the
whole family self-masks when it uses $N_{:,c}$ instead.
